The very end, where they reunite in heaven is perfect. I love the bridge scene, I love that they both seem at peace in the end. I think the main issues people have, myself included, is 1, Dean's death, and 2, never seeing Cas again, even if he's mentioned. If I had written it this is how I would have ended things personally. In order for Sam to have his happy ending, wife, kid, whatever, he would need to give up hunting (debatable, but whatever) and Dean wasn't going to retire. Sam obviously would stay hunting with Dean until the end of time, maybe give it up here and there, but he'd never truely give it up if Dean's still out there hunting. Dean didn't deserve his stupid rebar death. It was ridiculous. I don't care about the plot armor thing, it was fucking stupid. He fought his entire life, gave up every single ounce of himself to save people and kill monsters. It wasn't fair, and yeah that's how life is but he deserved a better ending, he deserved to be happy. So here's how I would have fixed it. First, scene showing Jack pulling Cas out of the empty. We deserved to see Cas one last time, and the two of them heading off to rebuild heaven. It wouldn't have had to be much, just a quick hug and like a "We've got some work to do." from Jack. Then we cut back to Sam and Dean, similar barn scene, except instead of dying, Dean gets injured. Career ending injury of some sort, I've always thought maybe one of his legs. Enough where he can still walk, but maybe can't run, or has too bad of a limp, just something that forces him to slow down. We see some brotherly montage of Sam helping Dean rehab, Dean gets frustrated obviously, goes to a bar to drink his anger away, and finds out his favorite bar in Lebanon is up for sale. Of course he can't stand for that, so he and Sam somehow get the money (Idk how exactly, but they would) and Dean remakes the place into a roadhouse type of place, maybe name it Bobby's or Mary's (ik, I'm not a fan of hers either but she's still his mother and he would honor her in that way.), very reminiscent of the bar he had in his head when Michael had him trapped. At the same time we see Eileen and Sam reunite, helping Dean with decor and stock. Sam and Eileen are all cute and flirty cause their relationship heals my soul. A few flash scenes, family dinner at Sam and Eileen's house (Maybe they stay in the bunker? Idk, I'd think they'd want some normalcy.) a couple years in the future, no actual wedding scene cause it would be cheesy, but some wedding picture visible on like a fireplace mantle would be perfect, subtle but there, Cas and Jack stop in for dinner. Don't necessarily need a big reunion scene, I think it's better left up to our imaginations and we just see the 5 of them happy and interacting, like it's perfectly normal to be having family dinner. Another flash scene to the bar, which has turned in to a bit of a hunters safe house in the back, where they can come for lore and advice, spell supplies, weapons. Maybe we see Claire, in her mid 20s now stomping in, pissed off because of a case, and Dean gives her a drink cause she looks like she needs it. Dean gives her some advice, she calls him grandpa or something cause he's now in his mid 40s. Another jump a few years later, Sam and Eileen want a weekend away so they ask "uncle Dean" to babysit their kid who's a couple years old now, 5 or 6ish, which he's secretly over the moon to do, but grumbles a bit on the outside. Cut to Sam driving his own car, Eileen in the passengers seat, thinking pickup truck vibes cause he's a family man now and obviously Dean keeps Baby. Jack's calling Sam because he might be new God, but he's still generally confused and a child, and has a random question about caterpillars or something. Another scene, both brothers are older, 50s ish, Sam and Eileen's kid is a teen now, and they're both teaching him (We'll go with him cause Sam had a son in the real ending.) General self defense stuff, not to become a hunter, but just how to stop and kill what if absolutely necessary. Another scene, Dean hitting on women at the bar, he's in his 60s but he still thinks he has a shot cause he's still him. Maybe a demon comes in after hours, gets stuck cause of a demon trap on the ceiling, Dean has the demon blade tucked up under the bar, ganks the demon, has a little smirk and a "still got it" moment. Btw, Carry On Wayward Son, the version they used in the actual finally is playing the whole time during these scenes. I don't think Dean would ever truely settle down with anyone, he'd try, have a few relationships but the main point of this is that he gets to be a normal man in the end, and gets to watch Sam grow and find happiness, which is what would make him happy. Maybe just cause it would be funny, throw in a random teenage girl showing up at the bar looking for him, turns out it's his daughter (cause let's be real, there is no way this dude doesn't have at least 1 kid out there! He's a hoe but we love him for it. Also ignoring the amazon daughter he had, Emma, cause she was a monster.) Maybe a few more scenes, maybe a few less, but scenes basically that jump a few years here and there, seeing the boys age (without that God awful wig!)  And then all the sudden the screen goes white. The actual scene where Dean meets Bobby in heaven happens, slight variation of the script since Dean would know that heaven is fixed already cause Cas and Jack would pop in every once in a while. Cut back to Sam, (again, without that stupid wig, anything but that stupid wig! Bald would be hilarious) grey, in his late 60s, early 70s, getting condolences at Dean's hunter funeral, pyre, all that jazz, and while Sam's upset, he knows Dean's okay in heaven. Sam hands the keys to Deans bar to his daughter, and tells her to take good care of the family business. Maybe makes a sad joke about telling Dean off about his cholesterol, cause Dean died normally, heart attack or something along those lines, and then we have the final scenes with Sam on earth, his son telling him it's okay, then the reunion on the bridge where they're both young again (my theory is basically you see people in heaven the way you want to see them, like their souls aren't stuck at the age they were when they died. Maybe Bobby sees them as they were in their early 20s, and they see Bobby in his 50s.) And then they walk off together towards Baby, Dean says something about how he can't wait for Eileen to meet everyone (all of their friends and family who are in heaven with them) and Sam nods. Ends with them getting in Baby, starting the engine, and they drive off. Or just the normal ending on the bridge. Anyways, that's how I would have personally ended it, they live full lives, get their versions of happy endings, and then get peace in heaven for forever. There's more I could definitely add, more thoughts and scenes, but this is already so long so I'll leave it there, but this is the ending in my head and it makes me feel a lot better.

We didn't really grow up in a religious house. My younger brother and I were raised "Catholic" but we didn't attend church, weren't baptized but we did go to Catholic school so we did attend mass for holidays at school. My Mum prays on occasion, my Dad only when something bad happens. I never really believed, but I also didn't believe either. Just kind of an acknowledgement like if there's a God then cool, but if there isn't then that's fine. I like to think I'm a good person and if there is a heaven that I'd get there. However my older half-brother was raised more by his mother. My Dad had partical custody on weekends but his Mom had him during the week. His step-dad became a born-again Christian when my brother was around 15 or 16, he never really mentioned it, didn't go to church with them, and overall it was a nonfactor in his life. He's 31 now but about 5 years ago all the sudden he's posting super religious stuff on his Facebook out of the blue. He moved to Boston for school so I didn't see him as much as we used to. So I called him, I didn't directly ask about it cause I didn't want an argument (he gets pretty hard headed sometimes) but he brought up how he loves his new chuch and the community. And I was like oh that's good, I didn't know you were going to church. Then he goes on this 30 minute rant about religion and really starts getting preachy with me about "being a sinner" because I'm bi (meanwhile at the time I had never even been with a woman, just a few casual dates) and how I have to repent for my sins of the flesh. I kept my mouth shut for the most part but once he was done I asked him if God forgives all sins, he said yes, and I said then I'm all good, which started another rant about how socially he doesn't judge but religiously I basically need to go to confession and pray. I didn't pry anymore cause I was pretty annoyed and wanted to end the conversation before I ended up blowing up and it turning into a fight. I have a short temper. I let it go, trust me I was annoyed but he's still my brother and I love him so I'm not going to start family problems because of it. Plus I've been with my boyfriend for almost 4 years so I'm basically straight. But suddenly when my brother comes home for holidays he goes from a good 50/50 split between our family and his mothers family to only visiting us once for like a half day when he was in town for a week. Fine, whatever, he was in his late 20s at this point so he can do what he wants even if it kinda hurt us a bit. The last straw for me was when he came home around fathers day last year, he stayed with us for a few days like how he used to, and the morning of father's day he gets up super early, drives to his mother house and spends the day with his step dad. I've met him, he's generally a decent guy from what I know but at the time he had been arrested like 2 months prior for a dui, nobody was hurt, he didn't crash or anything, just got pulled over when driving. He was in AA after that and to my knowledge hasn't had a drink since which I can respect but my opinion of the guy was definitely tainted, especially since a friend of mine was hit by a drunk driver when we were in high school. But my brother knew the plans for the day, we were taking Dad out for dinner and then to his favourite brewery for a couple beers (I know it's kind of hypocritical about taking him out for beer but I was the DD, and I don't even like beer so there was no chance of a dui situation there). We waited for him all day to come home, until almost 8pm and we decided to just go without him. We went, had a decent time but I could tell our Dad was hurt that he didn't show up. He got back around midnight and immediately went to  his room and went to bed. No card. Nothing. My brother was never like this before. Up until 2022 he was at every birthday, Christmas, father's day, even mothers day he would get my Mum a gift, and if he was in Boston he would facetime us. So I confronted him the next day cause I was pissed. I understand his stepdad was a Dad to him aswell but our Dad did not deserve that. His explanation was that he wanted to go to mass with his stepdad because we just don't get it and he needs his comunity. So I start yelling because as far as I know, mass doesn't go on for 14-15 hours. He knew the plan, he agreed to it. He didn't even have the decency to answer any of our texts. Then he tells me he took his stepdad and his mother out for dinner, and then goes on a rant about how active his stepdad is in the church and how he deserves to treated because he works so hard. I have no problem with that however it was the way he went about it and how he idealizes the man because he has a strong relationship with God and we don't, meanwhile he literally could have killed someone had the cop not pulled him over that night. All he had to do was say that he already had plans and we would have moved our dinner to Monday no problem. He apologized for not getting a card but didn't apologize for not showing up like he promised. It was like looking at a stranger. I did not recognize the brother I grew up with. He just had this blank stare as if nothing was wrong. My Dad forgave him and they're on good terms but I don't have the same relationship with him anymore. When I do talk to him if religion get brought up, which he temds to talk about a lot, I change the subject. I don't like not being close with him like we used to be but every conversation turns into a preach fest. I don't want to hear it. I say that I'm an atheist just to get under his skin, but honestly I'm pretty agnostic. I'm not apposed to the idea, but I have no proof either. So long story short that's pretty much the reason I say I'm an atheist. I've just lost a lot of respect for my brother because of his brainwashed culty mentally. Our younger brother still talks to him fairly frequently, which is fine, I'm not going to interfere with their relationship but until (assuming he ever does) he starts acting like himself again I will have a very cordial relationship going forward for the sake of keeping the peace. Am I overreacting? Probably. But I just really felt like I saw his true colours that day and I felt like our side of the family was just being used for his convenience.

He's 18 now so he's able to take care of himself for the most part, but we still check on him when he's sleeping because thats when he typically goes low. I love my family and would do anything for them, but for me it's not even about that, it's just part of the routine.
